title: Linguistic and Cognitive Development through Imaginative Play
summary: This lesson addresses "linguistic and cognitive development through imaginative play" for children from two to three years old. Encourage him to engage in imaginative play; for example, give him a spoon so he can pretend to feed his stuffed toy, and take turns role-playing. This develops his communication skills and symbolic thinking. Let him play with some of the adults' clothes, like shoes, hats, and shirts, as this helps him begin role-playing and imaginative play, which nurtures his cognitive abilities. Provide him with items that stimulate his imagination, such as pots, pans, or building blocks, so he can pretend to cook. Join him in imaginative play and talk to him as if you are eating the food he pretended to cook.

reflection_prompts: My child is a year and a half old, and I want to develop his linguistic and cognitive skills through play. How do I start?
